upsc_summary: ISRO successfully launched the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission, injecting the NVS-03 satellite into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
NVS-03 is the 3rd of 5 planned second-generation navigation satellites (NVS series) designed to augment and sustain the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC).
Payload & Frequency Bands: NVS-03 operates across L1, L5, and S frequency bands. The addition of the L1 signal enhances interoperability with civil GNSS systems like GPS.
Indigenous Atomic Clock: Carries an indigenously developed Rubidium atomic clock alongside imported clocks to provide accurate timing references critical for positioning.
NavIC Capabilities: Provides Standard Positioning Service (SPS) for civilian users and encrypted Restricted Service (RS) for strategic users, covering India and a 1,500 km region beyond its borders.
Launch Vehicle: GSLV is a 3-stage vehicle featuring an indigenous Cryogenic Upper Stage (LOX/LH2 propellants) and liquid strap-on boosters (L-40).

title: The cumulative exports (merchandise & services) during April-October 2026-27 are estimated at US$ 568.84 Billion, as compared to US$ 487.59 Billion in April-October 2025-26, an estimated growth of 16.66%.
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: India's total cumulative exports (Merchandise and Services combined) for April-October 2026-27 reached US$ 568.84 Billion, registering a growth of 16.66% over US$ 487.59 Billion during April-October 2025-26.

Cumulative merchandise exports during April-October 2026-27 stood at US$ 309.06 Billion against merchandise imports of US$ 527.21 Billion, resulting in a merchandise trade deficit of US$ 218.15 Billion.
Estimated services exports during April-October 2026-27 stood at US$ 259.78 Billion against imports of US$ 134.98 Billion, generating a services trade surplus of US$ 124.80 Billion.
Top export destinations by value growth during April-October 2026-27 included the USA (14.48%), Singapore (107.5%), China (37.71%), Malaysia (106.87%), and Spain (88.38%).
Top import sources with highest growth during the same period included China (30.62%), Russia (54.83%), USA (27.63%), Oman (202.32%), and Brazil (144.54%).

title: CCPA Imposes ₹10 Lakh Penalty on Ola for Pre-Ride ‘Tip’ Feature; Directs Platform to Discontinue Practice
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 1:04PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) penalized cab-aggregator Ola ₹10 lakh for soliciting pre-ride 'tip'/'add-on' payments, declaring it an unfair trade practice and a dark pattern.

The practice was held to violate Section 2(47) (unfair trade practice) and Section 2(28)(iv) (concealment of material information) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, alongside Clause 14.15 of Motor Vehicles Aggregators Guidelines, 2025.

CCPA identified the UI mechanism as 'Confirm Shaming' under the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, which exploits consumer vulnerability by creating a false impression of ride delays without additional payment.

date:

upsc_summary: SHATAYU Portal: Launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment as a centralized national Geriatric Caregiver Dashboard and Directory to bridge the gap between trained caregiving professionals and elderly citizens.
Key Features: Provides location-based searchable caregiver profiles, OTP-based verification, request callbacks, and user rating mechanisms.
Professional Framework: Recognises four training categories—Geriatric Care Provider, Geriatric Caregiver, Wellness Therapist (Elderly), and Elderly Care Companion—supported by NISD and NSDC.
Significance for Care Economy: Enhances formal employment pathways for skilled caregivers while facilitating specialized elderly care (post-surgical, dementia, palliative, and mobility assistance).

title: Inviting feedback and suggestions on the Report submitted by Committee on Knowledge Systems
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 2:40PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: Committee on Knowledge Systems: Chaired by Ratan P. Watal, the committee submitted its report to MoSPI outlining an actionable policy paper on measuring the contribution of knowledge and knowledge products to the Indian economy.

Measurement Framework: Recommends developing a family of System of National Accounts (SNA 2025)-consistent thematic statistics/accounts rather than a single aggregate measure for the Knowledge Ecosystem.
Priority Thematic Accounts: Focuses on Human Capital, R&D, Creative Economy, AI Systems, Data & Databases, High-Tech Products, and the Digital Economy.

Federated Implementation Model: Distributes measurement responsibilities across System Integrators (MoSPI), Domain Institutions (sectoral ministries), and Key Partners (State Governments, academia, and regulatory bodies).

upsc_summary: PLI Scheme Performance: Covers 14 strategic sectors with an approved outlay of ₹1.91 lakh crore. As of June 2026, cumulative actual investments exceeded ₹2.58 lakh crore, generating over ₹23.79 lakh crore in production/sales and ₹15.53 lakh crore in exports.
Employment Impact: Created over 14.57 lakh direct and indirect jobs across key sectors including IT hardware, electronics, and solar PV modules.

Key Sectoral Outcomes: Electronics production reached ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025-26); mobile phone production rose 33x to ₹6.27 lakh crore, making India the 2nd largest mobile manufacturer with 99.2% domestic market usage; mobile phone imports dropped nearly 77%.

Strategic Import Substitution: Enabled first-time domestic manufacturing of 191 bulk drugs; targeted 50 GWh ACC battery storage capacity and awarded 48,337 MW integrated solar PV manufacturing capacity.

upsc_summary: Installed Renewable Capacity: Total power capacity reached ~560 GW, with non-fossil installed capacity reaching 308 GW (55% of total). India ranks 3rd globally in installed renewable energy capacity.
